1  SR. PP. SMT. BINDU.O.V  THIS CRIMINAL MISC. CASE HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 26.03.2026, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY PASSED THE FOLLOWING:
 2026:KER:27113 CRL.M.C.NO.1415 OF 2022  3  ORDER Dated this the 26th day of March, 2026 The accused in Crime No.736/2017 of Kozhinjampara police station now pending as S.C.No.116/2018 on the file of the Fast Track Special Court, Palakkad, filed this Crl.M.C. under Section 482 Cr.P.C. praying for quashing all further proceedings against him.
2. The offences alleged against the petitioner are under Sections 376(n) IPC and Sections 5(j)(II)(L)
& 6 of PoCSO Act.
3.

The prosecution case is that the accused after making friendship with the defacto complainant aged 17 and after promising to marry her committed penetrative sexual assault upon her on one day in June 2017 and thereafter on 16.07.2017 and 15.08.2017, impregnated her and thereby he is alleged to have committed the aforesaid offences.
4. According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, this is a false case foisted against the petitioner.
Moreover, relying upon Annexure 2 FSL report, the learned counsel would argue that as per the said report the petitioner is not the father of the foetus of the victim.
2026:KER:27113 CRL.M.C.NO.1415 OF 2022 Therefore, the learned counsel prayed for quashing all further proceedings against the petitioner.
5. The petition was strongly opposed by the learned Public Prosecutor.
Though notice was served on the defacto complainant/3rd respondent she did not turn up.
6. The specific case of the prosecution is that the petitioner after promising to marry the defacto complainant committed rape upon her and impregnated her.
However, from Annexure 2 FSL report it is revealed that 'the alleged father Sujay to whom the sample in item no.1(a) belongs is excluded from the paternity of the foetus of Divya in item no.3'.
From the above result, it is conclusively proved that the petitioner is not the biological father of the foetus of the defacto complainant.
Therefore, the prosecution case that the petitioner impregnated the defacto complainant has no legs to stand and as such there is no meaning in forcing the petitioner to face the trial.
In the result, this Crl.M.C. is allowed.

All further proceedings in Crime No.736/2017 of Kozhinjampara police station now pending as 2026:KER:27113 CRL.M.C.NO.1415 OF 2022 S.C.No.116/2018 on the file of the Fast Track Special Court, Palakkad, stands quashed under Section Sujay vs State Of Kerala on 26 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107044009/
